scheme_name: PMMSY: Establishment of small RAS /Biofloc culture system - Haryana
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on September 10, 2020. 

The scheme aims to bring about the holistic development of the fisheries sector in India. 

It focuses on enhancing fish production and productivity in a sustainable manner. 

The PMMSY is particularly significant for states like Haryana, which have a growing interest in aquaculture. 

The establishment of small Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS) and Biofloc culture systems is a key component of this initiative. 

The objective of the PMMSY is to increase fish production to 22 million metric tonnes by 2024-2025. 

This represents a substantial increase from the 13.7 million metric tonnes produced in 2018-2019. 

The scheme also aims to create an additional employment opportunity for 55 lakh people in the fisheries sector. 

The PMMSY has a financial outlay of ₹20,050 crores for a period of five years. 

Out of this, ₹9,000 crores are allocated for the development of marine fisheries, while ₹11,000 crores are for inland fisheries and aquaculture. 

In Haryana, the focus on small RAS and Biofloc systems is particularly relevant due to the limited availability of water resources. 

These systems are designed to optimize water usage and increase fish production per unit area. 

The Biofloc technology allows for the cultivation of fish in a controlled environment, reducing the need for water exchange. 

This technology can lead to a production of 20 to 30 tonnes of fish per hectare per year. 

The financial assistance provided under the PMMSY for setting up small RAS and Biofloc systems can be up to 60% of the project cost. 

For SC/ST and women beneficiaries, this assistance can go up to 80% of the project cost. 

The maximum limit for financial assistance for small RAS systems is ₹20 lakhs. 

For Biofloc systems, the maximum limit is ₹10 lakhs. 

The eligibility criteria for beneficiaries include being a resident of Haryana and having a minimum age of 18 years. 

The applicant must also possess basic knowledge of aquaculture practices. 

A minimum educational qualification of Class 8 is required for applicants. 

The application process for the PMMSY involves several steps. 

First, interested beneficiaries must submit an application to the Fisheries Department of Haryana. 

The application form can be obtained from the official website or the local fisheries office. 

Applicants must provide documents such as identity proof, address proof, and bank account details. 

A project report detailing the proposed aquaculture system must also be submitted. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the Fisheries Department. 

The department will conduct a site visit to assess the feasibility of the proposed project. 

If approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed in a phased manner. 

The first installment is typically released after the project is initiated. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the progress of the project. 

The PMMSY also emphasizes capacity building and skill development for beneficiaries. 

Training programs are conducted to educate beneficiaries about modern aquaculture practices. 

These programs are organized by the Fisheries Department in collaboration with various institutions. 

The PMMSY aims to promote sustainable fishing practices and responsible aquaculture. 

It encourages the use of environmentally friendly technologies in fish farming. 

The scheme also supports the establishment of fish markets and value-added processing units. 

This is intended to enhance the income of fish farmers and improve their livelihoods. 

The implementing authority for the PMMSY in Haryana is the Fisheries Department of the Government of Haryana. 

The department is responsible for the overall coordination and implementation of the scheme. 

For any queries or assistance, beneficiaries can contact the Fisheries Department at their official helpline number. 

The PMMSY is expected to significantly contribute to the economic development of Haryana. 

It aims to empower local communities by providing them with sustainable livelihood options. 

The scheme aligns with the broader goals of the Government of India to promote self-reliance in the fisheries sector. 

The PMMSY also emphasizes the importance of research and development in aquaculture. 

It encourages partnerships between government agencies, research institutions, and private sector players. 

The scheme is a part of the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative, which aims to make India self-sufficient. 

The PMMSY is expected to foster innovation in aquaculture practices. 

It aims to create a robust framework for the growth of the fisheries sector in Haryana. 

The scheme also addresses the challenges of climate change and water scarcity. 

By promoting efficient aquaculture systems, the PMMSY aims to ensure food security. 

The scheme is expected to enhance the nutritional security of the population by increasing fish availability. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive approach to developing the fisheries sector in India. 

It integrates various aspects such as production, processing, marketing, and export. 

The focus on small RAS and Biofloc systems is particularly relevant in the context of Haryana's agricultural landscape. 

These systems can be implemented in small spaces, making them accessible to small and marginal farmers. 

The PMMSY is a significant step towards achieving sustainable development in the fisheries sector. 

It aims to create a vibrant aquaculture ecosystem that benefits all stakeholders involved. 

The scheme is a testament to the Government of India's commitment to enhancing the livelihoods of fish farmers. 

Through the PMMSY, the government aims to transform the fisheries sector into a key driver of economic growth. 

The establishment of small RAS and Biofloc culture systems under the PMMSY is a forward-thinking initiative. 

It has the potential to revolutionize fish farming in Haryana and contribute to the overall development of the region.
